 Coram:
 Justice G. Satapathy
 Order(Oral)
Order No. 11.12.2024
 02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is a bail application U/S.483 of BNSS, 2023 by the Petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Saintala P.S. Case No. 305 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.292 of 2024 pending in the f i l e o f l e a r n e d J M F C , S a i n t a l a f o r c o m m i s s i o n o f o f f e n c e s p u n i s h a b l e U / S s 498-A/294/376/323/506/34 of IPC r/w Sec. 4 of DP Act, on the allegation of committing rape upon the victim as well as subjecting her to torture and cruelty for demand of dowry along with co-accused.
3. Heard, Mr. Kirtan Dang, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. B.P. Nayak, learned Additional Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record.

4. It is not disputed that the marriage of the Informant with the brother of the Petitioner was solemnized on 09.04.2023, but it is alleged in the FIR that after 15 days of the marriage, the Petitioner has allegedly committed rape upon the victim, however, the FIR has been lodged against the Petitioner and others after near about 1 year and 3 months on 19.07.2024.

The delay in lodging of FIR is of course a ground for embellishment, but in a case like this, where the accused, who is the relative of the victim of rape has been alleged to have committed rape upon his sister-in- law(wife of brother-in-law), delay in lodging of FIR may be natural owing to various reason of social stigma and family pressure, however, such delay is a factor to be considered in the trial, but not at this stage of consideration of bail application, since no finding can be arrived at, at such stage.

sentences.text:
In view of the above facts and after having considered the rival submissions and taking into account the nature and gravity of offence as alleged against the Petitioner vis--vis the accusations sought to be brought against him and regard being had to the materials placed on record in entirety,
this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the Petitioner at this stage, when the victim is yet to be examined in the trial.
Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands rejected.
6. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
